reason: The text explicitly demonstrates collaboration between leaders and people throughout. The leaders are identified (Zerubbabel, Jeshua the High Priest, priests, and Levites), and the people gather 'as one man' (כְּאִישׁ אֶחָד) to Jerusalem. The leaders take initiative in building the altar and organizing the temple work, while the people collectively participate. The leadership allocates resources ('they gave silver to the stonecutters and carpenters') enabling communal work. Crucially, both leaders and people participate together in the religious observances: the priests and Levites lead the worship with musical instruments while 'all the people shouted a great shout in praise' (וְכָל־ הָעָם הֵרִיעוּ תְרוּעָה גְדוֹלָה) at the temple's foundation-laying. The entire narrative portrays coordinated, unified action toward the shared goal of rebuilding the temple.
